pairs: The understanding of the sons of Korah.
Quemadmodum desiderat cervus ad fontes aquarum,
As the deer longs for fountains of water,
ita desiderat anima mea ad te,
so my soul longs for you,
Sitivit anima mea ad Deum fortem, vivum;
My soul has thirsted for the strong living God.
quando veniam, et apparebo ante faciem Dei?
When will I draw close and appear before the face of God?
Fuerunt mihi lacrimæ meæ panes die ac nocte,
My tears have been my bread, day and night.
Meanwhile, it is said to me daily:
et effudi in me animam meam,
quoniam transibo in locum tabernaculi admirabilis,
For I will cross into the place of the wonderful tabernacle,
all the way to the house of God,
with a voice of exultation and confession,
And why do you disquiet me?
for I will still confess to him:
Ad meipsum anima mea conturbata est:
My soul has been troubled within myself. Because of this,
propterea memor ero tui de terra Jordanis et Hermoniim a monte modico.
I will remember you from the land of the Jordan and from Hermon, from the little mountain.
with the voice of your floodgate.
et fluctus tui super me transierunt.
and your waves have passed over me.
In die mandavit Dominus misericordiam suam,
In the daylight, the Lord has ordered his mercy;
and in the night, a canticle to him.
apud me oratio Deo vitæ meæ.
With me is a prayer to the God of my life.
And why do I walk in mourning,
While my bones are being broken,
exprobraverunt mihi qui tribulant me inimici mei,
my enemies, who trouble me, have reproached me.
dum dicunt mihi per singulos dies:
Meanwhile, they say to me every single day,
And why do you disquiet me?
for I will still confess to him:
